text:
The attached foundation plan shows a 6 in CMU foundation wall, 4 ft high, with no openings. Use 8 in x 16 in (nominal) CMUs.
Q1. How many CMUs must be purchased, including 5 % waste?
Q2. If every cell is grouted, how many cubic yards of grout are needed, including 5 % waste? A fully grouted 6 in CMU takes 0.17 ft³ of grout.
Q3. If only the cells with vertical reinforcement at 32 in on center are grouted, how many cubic yards of grout are needed, including 5 % waste?
rules: Estimating conventions: total wall length = sum of the outside dimensions (no deduction at corners); wall area = length x height; one CMU covers 8 in x 16 in = 0.889 ft²; round CMUs up after adding waste. Grout = CMUs before waste x grout per CMU, converted to CY (27 ft³ = 1 CY), then add grout waste. Cells are 8 in apart, so grouting at S in on center fills 8/S of the cells.

text:
The attached diagram shows a gable roof with a 7:12 slope.
Q1. What is the net roof area (ft²)?
Q2. How many rolls of #15 single-coverage underlayment (144 ft x 3 ft per roll) are needed? The underlayment laps 4 in under each rake edge and overlaps 1 ft at the ridge.
Q3. The roof is covered with 3-tab asphalt strip shingles, 3 ft x 1 ft, with 5.5 in exposure. Find (a) the starter-course area at the eaves (ft²), (b) the area for the 1 ft ridge coverage (ft²), (c) the cutting-waste area at the rakes (ft², 0.25 ft² per linear foot of rake), (d) the gross roof area (ft²), and (e) the number of shingles.
rules: Estimating conventions: run = half the eave-to-eave distance; rise = run x slope; rake length = sqrt(run² + rise²); net roof area = rake length x eave length x 2 roof planes. Underlayment area = net area + ridge lap (eave length x 1 ft) + rake laps (4/12 ft x rake length x 4 rake edges); rolls = area / (roll length x width), rounded up. Starter course = eave length x exposure x 2 eaves; ridge coverage = eave length x 1 ft; rake waste = 4 rake edges x rake length x 0.25 ft²/ft; gross area = net + starter + ridge + rake waste; shingles = gross area / (3 ft x exposure), rounded up.
